subject: 🏃 Tuesday — Threshold + Max-HR Test (Wk 6)
html:
Tomorrow: Home-Hills Threshold (3 × 5 min) + H10 Max-HR Test — evening session, ≤60 min total. Solo-parenting week means no morning slot; housekeeper arrives 4:30 PM, so you're out the door ~4:35. No track drive — this runs from home on your hilly west-side roads, HR-governed throughout.

The session: 5-min pre-run activation (quadruped hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus the PT-prescribed quadruped banded hip IR 5–10 reps each side). Then ~10 min easy warm-up jog from the door + 3–4 strides to open up. Threshold block: 3 × 5 min @ HR 155–165, cap 165 on a rolling/uphill stretch, 90s easy jog recovery between reps. Pace floats with the hills — HR is the only governor. That's ~15 min in threshold zone, trimmed from the original 4×1600 to fit the compressed window. Then 2 min easy jog. Max-HR test: 2 × ~75s all-out uphill efforts — build into the first one hard, walk back down, then the second one absolutely maximal to volitional exhaustion. Keep the watch recording and walk ~30s at the top to catch the peak. Then 8–10 min easy cooldown jog home.

Why this matters: every HR zone in the plan is anchored to an unconfirmed 180 placeholder — the cleanest H10 reads are two submaximal 167s, so the true max is genuinely unknown. This test pins the real number. Once confirmed, we recompute every zone band (easy, MP, threshold) at the correct percentages and the Presidio Pivot HR co-gate firms up. This is the single highest-leverage data point between now and race day.

Gates: knee 1/5 AM (Monday was 1/5 — set) and feeling fully recovered. Hard abort: chest tightness, dizziness, or unusual SOB at any point → stop immediately, jog home easy. The max effort should feel terrible but safe — legs burning, lungs screaming, but nothing alarming in the chest.

Focus cue: the second hill rep is the one that counts. The first rep is a rehearsal — go hard, not all-out. Save the absolute max effort for rep 2. Sprint until you physically cannot maintain pace, then keep the watch running for ~30s of walking to capture the post-effort peak. That smooth-climb peak is your real max HR.

Context: Week 6 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) — 47 days to the SF Marathon. You're coming off a clean Monday hip circuit (knee 1/5) and a strong Week 5 closer (12.75 mi long run with textbook HR discipline and a 7:27–7:29 MP fast-finish at HR 152–157). The unbroken knee-1/5 streak and the fitness readout from that long run say the engine is ready for this test. After tomorrow, every workout has real zones behind it instead of placeholder math.

Tonight: lay out your running kit and the H10 strap by the door. Hydrate well. Eat a normal dinner — nothing heavy, nothing experimental. Bed by 10. Tomorrow afternoon, double-check "Polar H10 — Connected" in Watch Settings → Bluetooth before stepping out. Post-run: read the peak HR from the Strava trace (or Polar Flow), confirm it's the top of a smooth climb and not a 1-sample artifact, and text me the number.
